ctx.x: I could be with her. Our first two children were born in the summertime, and they were delighted that they could have their birthday parties at Auntie Maro’s house, because they had friends in the neighborhood, and it was more fun than New York. So I got to not only sign some musicians – Turk Murphy lived in San Francisco. We were old friends from my seeing him when I went overseas and he was just about to go into the Navy with the entire Lu Watters band, which had to break up because of the war closing down…

items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: During his career he has produced albums with many of the greatest artists in jazz, including Miles Davis, Dave Brubeck and Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: Producer/historian George Avakian has played a major role in the development of jazz and popular music in America. He was born in Armenia in 1919 and immigrated with his family to the U.S. While a student at Yale, he produced the pioneering documentary jazz album “Chicago Jazz” while also entering the field of jazz journalism. During his career he has produced albums with many of the greatest artists in jazz, including Miles Davis, Dave Brubeck and Louis Armstrong. His writing on music has appeared in Down Beat,…
George was interviewed in Clinton, New York on April 21, 1998, by Monk Rowe, Director of the Fillius Jazz Archive.

items.title: Dave Brubeck — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Did that come from George Avakian?

ctx.x: Who suggested that? Did that come from George Avakian?

That came from me. My friend in the Army taught me all the Matt Dennis tunes. He was Festus in “Gunsmoke.” Ken Curtis. He could sing with the big bands and often took the place of Frank Sinatra or somebody. He was that good.
